past_medical_history: Dry eye syndrome (bilateral, on artificial tears — seronegative, prior anti-SSA/SSB negative 3 years ago)
family_history: Mother: type 2 diabetes, died stroke age 82. Father: no neurological disease. No family history of neuropathy or ataxia.

social_history.note: Retired administrative director for university hospital. Widowed. Non-smoker. Rare alcohol (wine, 1-2 glasses per week). No illicit drugs. Lives alone — falls are a safety concern.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4. MMSE 29/30. Normal cognition and language.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: CN II-XII intact. No nystagmus. Normal extraocular movements. Normal facial sensation. Hearing normal.
neurological_exam.motor: Motor strength full (5/5) throughout all four limbs. No fasciculations. Normal bulk.
neurological_exam.sensory: Vibration: absent at great toes bilaterally, severely reduced at ankles (0 seconds), reduced at knees (4 seconds). Proprioception: absent at great toes bilaterally, severely reduced at ankles. Light touch mildly reduced in feet bilaterally. Pinprick relatively preserved in feet. Hands: absent proprioception at distal phalanges bilaterally, absent vibration at fingers.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps 1+ bilaterally. Patellar absent bilaterally. Achilles absent bilaterally. Brachioradialis trace bilaterally.
neurological_exam.coordination: Severe dysmetria on finger-nose bilaterally — PSEUDOATHETOSIS of outstretched hands with eyes closed. Positive Romberg (falls within 5 seconds of eye closure). Heel-shin moderately impaired bilaterally.
neurological_exam.gait: Wide-based ataxic gait. Stomping quality to steps. Falls in tandem walk. Dramatically worsens with eye closure (sensory ataxia).
neurological_exam.special_tests: Pseudoathetosis present (hands move involuntarily with eyes closed). No Babinski. No clonus. Lhermitte's sign negative.

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive sensory loss and imbalance over 2 years, ataxic gait, no pain
patient.history_present_illness: Patricia Osei is a 63-year-old retired administrative director presenting with a 2-year history of progressive gait instability and sensory changes in her feet and hands. Unlike many neuropathy presentations, she has minimal pain — her predominant complaint is a profound sense of unsteadiness that she likens to 'walking on a cushion of air.' She has had two significant falls in the past 6 months, both in the dark or when closing her eyes in the shower. She has noticed increasing difficulty with fine motor tasks including fastening buttons and picking up small objects, with a sense of losing track of where her fingers are without looking. Her balance is dramatically worse with eyes closed than open, and she uses a cane now. She was evaluated for inner ear problems twice — hearing is normal, and an ear specialist found no vestibular disorder. Her past medical history is notable for a 12-year history of well-controlled type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 6.8%) and a seronegative (anti-SSA/SSB negative) dry eye syndrome she has managed with artificial tears for 8 years. Neurological review of prior records reveals that previous neurologists noted reduced reflexes and attributed findings to diabetes, but the predominance of deep sensory loss and sensory ataxia over pain is considered atypical for typical diabetic neuropathy.

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: Glucose (random) 142 mg/dL (H), HbA1c 6.8 % (H), ANA 1:80 homogeneous titer (H), Anti-SSA (Ro) POSITIVE — 68 U/mL (H).

specialized_test.impression: ABNORMAL NCS/EMG — sensory neuronopathy pattern. Sensory nerve action potentials severely reduced or absent in both upper and lower extremities in a non-length-dependent, pan-extremity distribution. Motor nerve conduction studies normal. Needle EMG: no fibrillations, no chronic reinnervation changes. Findings localize to a disorder affecting sensory neurons above the level of the peripheral nerve, consistent with a sensory ganglionopathy

output.impression: Minor salivary gland biopsy: focus score 1 focus/4 mm². Lymphocytic sialadenitis present (periductal lymphocytic infiltrate, defined foci). Findings are consistent with lymphocytic sialadenitis

Autonomic testing: QSART bilateral feet absent (no sweat output — severe sudomotor loss). Orthostatic vitals: BP 138/80 supine → 122/74 at 3 min standing → 114/70 at 5 min standing (borderline orthostatic hypotension, not meeting diagnostic threshold of 20/10 mmHg drop). HRV: reduced variability. Findings suggest mild autonomic involvement.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Sjögren's syndrome-associated sensory neuronopathy (dorsal root ganglionopathy)

differential.key_features: Anti-Hu DRG involvement is the classic mimic; requires paraneoplastic panel and CT chest (esp. SCLC screen).
Diagnosis of exclusion once Sjögren's and paraneoplastic causes are ruled out.
Can mimic with proprioceptive ataxia; need B12, MMA, homocysteine; spinal MRI shows posterior column signal change.
Symmetric length-dependent axonal pattern; does not present as a sensory ganglionopathy with non-length-dependent loss.
Pyridoxine megadose causes sensory ganglionopathy; review supplement history.

optimal_actions.action: Order broad neuropathy labs (CBC, CMP, HbA1c, B12 + MMA, TSH, SPEP/IFE, urinalysis)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify reversible/treatable etiologies (diabetes, B12 deficiency, monoclonal gammopathy, thyroid disease)

optimal_actions.action: Order EMG/NCS to characterize axonal vs demyelinating pattern and distribution
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Length-dependent axonal vs demyelinating vs multifocal pattern; severity and distribution

optimal_actions.action: Search literature for DSP evaluation guidelines and etiology-specific recommendations
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirm AAN 2009 DSP workup, etiology-specific evaluations

optimal_actions.action: Review medications for neurotoxic agents and check interactions for symptomatic therapy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify potentially neurotoxic drugs (chemotherapy, metronidazole, megadose B6, nitrofurantoin); guide neuropathic-pain pharmacotherapy

optimal_actions.action: Sjögren's and paraneoplastic serologies (anti-SSA, anti-SSB, anti-Hu, anti-CV2, anti-amphiphysin, anti-PNMA, anti-Ri)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Anti-SSA/SSB supports Sjögren's; paraneoplastic antibodies support DRG-onconeural cause

optimal_actions.action: Minor salivary gland (lip) biopsy for Sjögren's confirmation; consider skin biopsy for IENFD if small-fiber overlap is suspected
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Reduced IENFD supports small-fiber component; lip biopsy (flagged as off-vocab) confirms Sjögren's histologically

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is a cortical test and is non-contributory in peripheral nerve disease.
Head/brain CT has no role in peripheral neuropathy evaluation.
Brain MRI is not indicated in typical distal symmetric polyneuropathy without CNS signs.
Advanced cerebral imaging (PET/MRA/MRV/perfusion) has no routine role in peripheral neuropathy.
Echocardiography is not indicated unless cardiac amyloid is suspected.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is not indicated unless there is syncope or symptomatic dysautonomia with arrhythmia concern.

sequence_constraints.reason: Tier the workup — basic labs first, then targeted electrodiagnostic and tissue studies.

critical_actions: Recognize non-length-dependent sensory loss + sensory ataxia + areflexia = sensory neuronopathy / dorsal-root ganglionopathy
Obtain paraneoplastic antibody panel and screen for occult malignancy (CT chest, CA-125, mammogram)
Send Sjögren's serology and consider minor salivary gland biopsy if seronegative
Initiate immunotherapy (IVIG / steroids) if Sjögren's-associated and disabling
contraindicated_actions: Do not attribute to diabetic neuropathy without addressing the sensory-ataxic, non-length-dependent pattern
Do not delay malignancy screen — anti-Hu paraneoplastic causes are a critical alternative
key_reasoning_points: Sensory loss in a NON-length-dependent pattern with sensory ataxia and areflexia points to DRG (ganglionopathy), not peripheral nerve
Sjögren's is the most common identifiable cause of sensory ganglionopathy; sicca features here support workup
Anti-Hu paraneoplastic ganglionopathy is the must-not-miss alternative

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Well-controlled diabetes does not produce a sensory ganglionopathy pattern.

red_herrings.intended_effect: Dismiss Sjögren's because of remote negative serology
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Anti-SSA/SSB seroconversion occurs; up to 30% of Sjögren's cases are seronegative — lip biopsy is the gold standard if clinically suspected.
